text:
Logan Wright: kicking off the agg strategy debate here so we can settle it this week. question: do we ship hourly rollups, daily rollups, or both for route/model cost drivers? we need console “top routes” to feel fresh but also not be wildly off vs invoice.

Nadia Rahman: +1. metering events aren’t perfectly ordered. we see late arrivals regularly (esp streaming + retries). if we only do hourly, we’ll be constantly rewriting buckets.

Mei Lin: if we only do daily, the console is going to feel “dead” for last 24h. PM asked for “what changed week-over-week” and also people will look at “today” during incidents.

Chloe Martin: from console perspective: we need last 24h view to be responsive. doesn’t have to be perfect to the cent, but can’t be off by like 30%.

Allison Grant: SRE angle: hourly tables will increase compute + more frequent jobs = more ways to fail. also what’s our freshness SLO? (if we say 15m but data lags 2h, we’ll page ourselves).

Thomas Baird: cardinality angle: hourly partitions x route x model x region x env = lots of small files/partitions. we need to be careful not to create a “million partitions” problem.

Logan Wright: current proposal (rough):
- hourly rollups for recent window (e.g. last 48h)
- daily rollups for longer windows (e.g. 90d)
- console queries stitch hourly+daily depending on time range
Thoughts?

Mei Lin: that’s the classic pattern. we can have:
- agg_usage_route_model_hourly (partition by hour)
- agg_usage_route_model_daily (partition by day)
and a view that UNION ALLs them with a cutoff.

Nadia Rahman: but we still need to handle late metering. we have events arriving >2h late, sometimes ~24h late when a customer gateway buffers.

Caleb Johnson: latency/error telemetry has similar late arrival. we solved with watermark + correction window. basically we keep hourly buckets “mutable” for N hours, then freeze.

Jada Williams: mutable aggregates means upserts. do we have a clean upsert story in the warehouse? (or are we doing “delete partition then re-insert”)

Mei Lin: easiest: reprocess full hour partition for last N hours. delete+insert per (org_id, project_id, hour) partition if our storage supports it, otherwise overwrite partition files.

Allison Grant: what’s N? if N is 24h, that’s a lot of churn.

Nadia Rahman: data we pulled last month: p95 late arrival ~70m, p99 ~6h. long tail at 24h exists but rare (and mostly Dedicated customers with weird batching). maybe set N=8h for hourly “mutable window”, and accept that super-late events show up in daily recompute.

Chloe Martin: ok so “today” graph might shift a bit as late events land, but that’s normal.

Thomas Baird: if we’re overwriting partitions frequently, can we keep the grouping dims minimal in hourly? like hourly by route/model only, and push region/env to filterable but maybe not pre-aggregated? (or we’ll explode.)

Mei Lin: product requirements want filters: time range, environment, region, org/project, deployment mode. If we don’t pre-aggregate those dims, query cost spikes.

Logan Wright: query budget on the API endpoint is tight. we can’t be scanning raw events for top routes.

Jada Williams: could do hourly with fewer dims but then have derived tables for “top routes by env/region”. but then it’s basically multiple hourly tables anyway.

Thomas Baird: ok then at least enforce route cardinality upstream (hashing/rollups) so we don’t end up with 500k distinct routes per org.

Nadia Rahman: +1. but back to late events: I propose:
- hourly aggregates: recompute last 8 hours every run (sliding window)
- daily aggregates: recompute last 3 days daily (to absorb stragglers + corrections)
and document “numbers may shift for up to 72h”.

Allison Grant: +72h is fine as long as we set expectations and SLO doesn’t pretend it’s real-time. we should define “freshness” as “data through T-2h is 99% complete” or similar.

Chloe Martin: console copy can say “Data updated ~hourly. Recent usage may be delayed.” Also we can put a “last updated” timestamp.

Mei Lin: export reports are trickier. finance will run exports for last month and expect it to match invoice-ish. should exports use daily aggregates only?

Logan Wright: good point. I’d rather exports query daily aggregates and refuse ranges that include “today” unless user acknowledges it’s partial.

Talia Benson: jumping in — PM is ok with export being “bounded + stable”. they were more worried about timeouts than perfect freshness.

Jada Williams: implementation detail: for the “stitching” API, we need to avoid double-counting on the cutoff boundary. define cutoff = start_of_today_utc? or now-48h?

Mei Lin: recommend now-48h rounded down to hour. then:
- hourly covers [cutoff, now)
- daily covers [range_start, cutoff)
If user selects a range entirely within last 48h, only hourly.

Caleb Johnson: same logic for latency/error stats. though percentiles don’t compose perfectly across windows; careful with p95 across daily+hourly.

Nadia Rahman: yup. for latency we likely compute percentiles per hour and then approximate across range with t-digest merge if we store sketches, or just show hourly chart with p50/p95 per bucket. for “single number p95 for range” we can query a precomputed sketch table.

Chloe Martin: for GA can we just show p50/p95 per bucket and avoid a “range p95” summary? less math headaches.

Logan Wright: ok scope that separately. this thread mainly cost. cost composes cleanly.

Thomas Baird: on backfill approach: when we introduce route dimension, do we backfill historical data? or only “available after Feb X”? backfill is expensive.

Mei Lin: my vote: backfill last 14 days for beta (so customers see something), and maybe 90d post-GA as a one-time job. but we need a kill switch.

Allison Grant: please yes to kill switch + rate limit. also schedule off-peak. we should have a runbook with “max warehouse slots” and a rollback plan.

Nadia Rahman: backfill job should be incremental by day partition. if it fails mid-way, resume without duplicating.

Jada Williams: idempotency: make backfill write to a temp table then swap? or write with a job_id and only “activate” once complete.

Mei Lin: simplest: write daily partitions with deterministic keys and overwrite partition. activation not needed. but for safety we can do:
1) compute into agg_usage_route_model_daily_tmp for day D
2) validate counts
3) replace partition in main table

Logan Wright: ok summarizing tentative decision:
- Ship BOTH hourly + daily aggregate tables.
- Hourly is “mutable” for last 8h (recompute sliding window).
- Daily recompute last 3 days daily (to absorb late events).
- API stitches hourly (last 48h) + daily (older).
- Exports prefer daily aggregates; warn/limit ranges that include recent window.
- Backfill: plan for last 14d for beta, optional larger backfill gated + runbook.

Chloe Martin: sounds good from console. can we add a “data completeness” badge if we know pipeline lag?

Allison Grant: yes but please base it on concrete metrics (event ingestion lag + agg job lag). don’t hand-wave.

Thomas Baird: action item: I’ll update cardinality guardrails doc to explicitly call out hourly x route issues + recommend stable naming.

Nadia Rahman: I’ll draft the late-arrival policy + suggested copy for “numbers may change for up to 72h”.

Mei Lin: I’ll sketch table schemas + partitioning and share in the dataset doc. also need to confirm retention (hourly 7d? 14d? daily 90d?).

Logan Wright: retention proposal: hourly keep 14d, daily keep 13 months (finance comparisons). but we can keep daily at 90d for v1 if storage is tight.

Allison Grant: 13 months is nice but please confirm privacy/retention policy first.

Talia Benson: I’ll sync with Security/Compliance on retention + export retention; will report back.

Logan Wright: cool. will post a short ADR-ish note in confluence once we finalize the numbers. :thumbsup:
